references.text: Amminadab is mentioned as the father of Nahshon, who was leader of the tribe of Judah. This confirms the lineage of Elisheba.
Nahshon, son of Amminadab, was chief of the sons of Judah. He was the brother of Elisheba, Aaron's wife.
The names of Aaron's sons: Nadab, the firstborn, Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar – the same sons mentioned here.
Aaron's sons Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar are mentioned in the genealogy.
Nadab and Abihu, Aaron's sons, offered unauthorized fire before the Lord and died.
Aaron's sons Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar are mentioned when they were to be consecrated for priestly service.
The lineage from Amminadab to Nahshon is confirmed in Chronicles, showing Elisheba's ancestry.
Aaron's children Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar are mentioned in the Levitical genealogy.
Aaron's sons and their fate are described – Nadab and Abihu died without children, while Eleazar and Ithamar served as priests.
Amminadab and Nahshon are mentioned in Jesus' genealogy, showing the connection to Elisheba's family.
Amminadab and Nahshon are mentioned in Jesus' lineage according to Luke.
The lineage from Perez to Nahshon and Amminadab, who was Elisheba's father and brother.
Places Aaron's sons within the broader genealogical context (sons of Amram) and confirms the names of the priestly line.
Connects Aaron's four sons directly to the organization of the priestly service and their division into courses.
Confirms the identity of Elisheba's father (Amminadab) and brother (Nahshon), linking the priestly line to the royal line of Judah.
